# How Do I Manage Farm Inspections and Corrective Actions?


You manage inspections by using a checklist for each type of inspection, whether internal, from a buyer, or from an authority, and by turning every finding into a corrective action with an owner, a deadline, and a verification step. On **Jestor** , this runs through **Forms** , a **Pipe** for actions, and **Tasks** .


Inspections reveal problems that need to be fixed. But once the visit is over, findings are easily forgotten, and the same issues return at the next inspection.


## What unfollowed findings cost


- The same non-conformities repeated at each inspection
- Corrective actions that nobody owns
- No evidence that issues were fixed
- Pressure from buyers or authorities when problems persist
- Time wasted on preparing for inspections without learning from them


## How inspection management works


- A **checklist** is used for each inspection type
- Findings are recorded with photos and severity
- Each finding becomes an action with an owner and a deadline
- Closure requires a verification and evidence


## Why Jestor fits this use case


- Problems are fixed instead of repeated
- Evidence supports buyers, certifiers, and authorities
- Managers see which actions are open or late
- This scales from one farm to many sites


Findings noted and forgotten Findings tracked to closure


Repeated problems Owners, deadlines, and evidence


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Can I use the same checklist for internal inspections?** Yes, checklists can be reused. More at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Can I see all overdue actions?** Yes, a filtered dashboard lists them.


**Can inspectors from buyers use a restricted view?** Yes, permissions can be set for external reviewers.
